paragraphs.text: Annotation for the DSH sidebar browser: render pages through a same-origin host proxy, then click an
element or drag a region and send the note into the conversation.
# dsh-annotated-browser
**Annotate a real web page, then send the notes straight into the conversation.** Pick an element, o
r drag a region when the thing you mean is several nodes; write what should change; press send. The
model receives the selector, the visible text and the rectangle — not a screenshot it has to guess a
del receives the selector, the visible text and the rectangle — not a screenshot it has to guess at.
**English** · 中文
## What it solves
Saying "change *this* bit" about a real web page needs two things: **seeing the page**, and **naming
the part you mean**. This plugin exists for those two things.
**More pages load properly.** Some sites declare through `X-Frame-Options` or a CSP `frame-ancestors
` that they must not be embedded. Those declarations apply to pages framed directly from the remote
URL, and this plugin does not take that route: it renders the page in headless Chromium on the host
and serves the executed HTML from the DSH origin, so embedding restrictions do not come into play an
d the page displays normally.
**The page becomes readable.** Because the rendered result is served from the DSH origin, the panel
and the page are **same-origin** — the precondition for annotation. Same-origin access to the DOM is
what makes these possible:
- click an element and get its **selector** (`#id`, `data-testid`, or a CSS path walked up through i

ecord the visible text, the element's position, and your note together;
- keep picking without stopp
ing, then send everything as **one message in the order you picked it**.
**It respects what you already have installed.** With `takeover: false` the plugin does not replace
the `browser` tab type: shortcuts, "open in system browser", history, and every other plugin that op
ens `browser` tabs keep behaving exactly as before. It *adds* a separate annotated tab and a hand-of
f button in the tab strip.
**A whole page in one turn.** Adding a note leaves you in picking mode, so you can keep going until
you press Esc. Notes collect into one list and go out as a single message — a page-wide review costs
one turn instead of a dozen.
**No detour when it is already same-origin.** A page served by this DSH itself (another plugin's pag
e, say) is framed directly: cookies intact, no extra Chromium pass.
**Honest when it cannot work.** If an address is only reachable from your own machine (a port mapped
locally, for example), the panel falls back to **load directly (read-only)**: the page still shows,
and it says plainly that annotation is unavailable instead of leaving you with a blank frame to puz
ays plainly that annotation is unavailable instead of leaving you with a blank frame to puzzle over.
## What it looks like

1. Right sidebar → **Browser** → type a URL.
2. Toolbar → **Annotate** (Esc leaves it): click an ele

ment, or hold and drag to frame a region.
3. Write the note → **Add to list**. Picking continues aut

omatically.
4. **Send to conversation** posts every note as one message, in the order you made them.
The collected list survives a reload: it is persisted per Session in `localStorage` until you clear
list survives a reload: it is persisted per Session in `localStorage` until you clear it or send it.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart `dsh web` once (the host half has to load) and refresh the GUI.
**This is the recommended one-liner.** It downloads a prebuilt 273 KB tarball from GitHub Releases —
no build step, no git history, no npm account. Verified end to end from a clean profile with no pro
xy configured: 9.4 s.
Two alternatives, if you prefer:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Requirement:** a Chromium-based browser on the host machine — Chrome, Chromium or Edge all work. I
t is auto-detected (common Windows / macOS / Linux paths, or `CHROME_PATH` / `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_P
ATH`). If detection fails, point at it explicitly:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Configuration
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `browserExecutable` | auto-detect | absolute path to Chrome/Chromium |
| `proxyServer` | empty | H

TTP proxy used to render the page, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:7890` |
| `timeoutMs` | `30000` | page-loa

d budget in milliseconds |
| `allowRemote` | `false` | accept proxy requests from non-loopback peers

(only for a DSH exposed directly on a LAN) |
| `takeover` | `true` | provide the `browser` tab type
itself, so pages open straight into the annotatable view; `false` keeps the stock browser and adds
the hand-off button instead |
## Languages
The panel follows the GUI language (**Settings → General**), switching live with no reload. English
and Chinese ship in the box; every string lives in `i18n.js`, so another language is one dictionary
hinese ship in the box; every string lives in `i18n.js`, so another language is one dictionary away.
## Limits
- Pages are rendered by headless Chromium and re-served. Login state and heavy interactive apps can

behave differently from a real browser.
- The proxied page is served from the DSH origin. Treat it a

s trusted-ish content: only browse sites you would open in the GUI itself.
- Cookies from your own b
rowser are not shared with the rendered page.
